To its right, a light blue dashed box illustrates the imagination mechanism, showing transitions between states ($s_t, s_{t+1}$) and memory/latent states ($M_t, M_{t+1}$) influenced by a 'Cut a tree' action. A legend within this box uses blue and red arrows to distinguish between short-term and long-term imagination. The bottom third of the slide contains two bullet points that explain the model's functionality, with key technical terms highlighted in dark red. A dark red footer bar runs across the bottom, displaying 'ICLR 2025 Oral' on the left, the paper's full title in the center, and the slide number '4' on the right.

The slide uses a two-column layout with a large, bold, dark red title at the top left, followed by a thin horizontal separator line. The left column features a visual diagram illustrating the affordance map generation process using Minecraft-style imagery. It shows an input image labeled 'o_t' and a text goal 'Cut a tree' labeled 'I'. A red bounding box on the main image is linked via a camera icon to a zoomed-in view of a tree. The right column contains four bullet points in a light gray font that describe the methodology: using a sliding bounding box, performing continuous zoom-ins, assessing relevance with a MineCLIP model, and fusing values into a comprehensive map. The bottom of the slide includes two small-text footnotes on the left and a solid dark red footer bar containing the conference name 'ICLR 2025 Oral', the paper title, and the slide number '6'.

The slide uses a two-column layout with a prominent title in bold dark red at the top left, separated from the content by a thin horizontal line. The left column is occupied by a complex technical diagram illustrating a multi-step process. It begins with a text prompt 'Cut a tree' and a Minecraft screenshot, showing a sliding bounding box and a zoom-in effect that produces a sequence of 16 frames. These frames are fed into a 'MineCLIP' model, which generates correlation scores (e.g., 0.60, 0.90, 0.15) for different image regions. These scores are then fused into a final heatmap labeled as an affordance map. The right column contains four bullet points in red text that explain the steps shown in the diagram: employing a sliding bounding box, executing continuous zoom-ins, assessing relevance using MineCLIP, and fusing values to generate the map. The bottom of the slide includes small-text citations on the left and a solid dark red footer bar containing the conference name 'ICLR 2025 Oral', the presentation title, and the page number '6'.

The slide features a large, bold, dark red title at the top left, underlined by a thin horizontal line. The main body is divided into two columns containing complex technical diagrams. The right column displays a temporal flowchart showing the interaction between an 'env' (environment, in green) and an 'agent' (in pink) across time steps t, t+1, and t+Δt, highlighting the use of a 'Multimodal U-Net' to generate affordance maps. Below these diagrams, a single bullet point with red-highlighted text explains the training of the U-Net module for efficiency. A small footnote is located at the bottom left. layout_structure.title_text: Affordance-Based Intrinsic Reward and Jumping Flag
layout_structure.layout_description: The slide features a large, bold red title at the top-left, underlined by a thin red horizontal line that spans the width of the slide. The main content is divided into two horizontal tiers. The upper tier contains visual diagrams: the left side shows a mathematical expression for a 'Mean' involving the element-wise product of an 'Affordance map' heatmap and a 'Gaussian matrix' heatmap; the right side presents a two-row flowchart comparing Minecraft 'Observation' screenshots to their 'Affordance map' heatmaps, leading to 'High kurtosis' (Jump checkmark) or 'Low kurtosis' (Jump cross) outcomes. The lower tier consists of two columns of text, each with a single bullet point. Key terms within the text, such as 'affordance map', '2D Gaussian matrix', and 'jumpy state transition', are highlighted in red. A dark red footer bar at the bottom contains 'ICLR 2025 Oral' on the left, the paper title 'Open-World Reinforcement Learning over Long Short-Term Imagination' in the center, and the page number '8' on the right.
